cover_headline: India's Middle Class Borrows Faster Than Incomes as Debt Hits Record
facts: Household borrowing surged 36% in the year through March, taking consumer debt to a record 46% of GDP, according to central bank data reported by Bloomberg
About 13% of household income in the year through March 2025 went to servicing debt, up from 10%-11% for much of the previous decade, according to CLSA estimates
Borrowing rose roughly four times as fast as disposable income in 2025-26, while average earnings for regular salaried workers rose less than 4% in real terms in the three years through 2025

quote.text: Monthly installments seem convenient at first, but you don't realize how quickly you can get sucked into a cycle of repayments.
quote.speaker: Navjot Singh

end.headline: India's Middle Class Borrows Faster Than Incomes as Debt Hits Record
end.line: Household borrowing surged 36% in a year to a record 46% of GDP, while debt service climbed to about 13% of income and real pay for salaried workers rose less than 4% over three years.
